v1_human_g3_constraints.c_3: must operate only with provided inputs, no external data
v1_human_g3_constraints.c_5: all inputs assumed to be reasonable and consistent

v1_human_g3_frs.fr_1: The system shall provide an algorithm function that evaluates resource allocation feasibility
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_2: The function shall accept input a set of available resources with limited capacities
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_4: each request shall specify the amount of resources required
v1_human_g3_frs.fr_5: the function shall determine whether the available resources are sufficient to satisfy all requests

v1_human_g3_goal: The system checks whether a set of resource requests can be satisfied.
v1_human_g3_input:
resources: Dict[str, Number], a dictionary mapping each resource name (cpu, mem) to its total available capacity where capacities are int or float (numeric)
requests: List[Dict[str, Number]]
A list of resource requests of the above

v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_1: at all times the total amount of resources allocated must not exceed the available capacity of that resource
v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_2: given the same set of available resources and requests, the function shall always return same feasibility result
v1_human_g3_invariants.inv_3: the function shall always return a boolean

v1_human_g3_neg_req.neg_req_1: The system shall not modify input data
v1_human_g3_neg_req.neg_req_2: The system shall not attempt to partially satisfy requests

v1_human_g3_output:
bool is returned
True if all requests can be satisfied
false otherwise
